name: Trademark Registration
meta_title: Trademark Registration Online in India | Protect Your Brand
meta_description: Register your brand name and logo with expert trademark search, correct class selection and filing. Use TM immediately. WhatsApp your brand details to start.
excerpt: Protect your brand name and logo with a professionally searched and filed trademark application.
intro: Your brand name is often your most valuable asset, and the only way to own it legally is trademark registration. Without it, anyone can copy your name, and worse, someone else can register it and stop you from using it.

Eaccountingcart runs a proper availability search, selects the correct classes and files your application, so you can start using the TM mark immediately and the R mark once registered. Share your brand name and logo on WhatsApp to begin today.
what: A trademark protects brand identifiers, names, logos, taglines, labels and even sounds, under the Trade Marks Act, 1999. Applications are filed with the Trade Marks Registry in one or more of 45 classes covering different goods and services. Registration gives you exclusive nationwide rights for ten years, renewable indefinitely.
who: Startups and businesses building a brand worth protecting
E-commerce sellers who need brand registry access on marketplaces
Established businesses that never formalised their brand rights
Individuals protecting personal brands, channels or product names
benefits: Exclusive Nationwide Rights
Registration gives you the sole right to use the mark across India in your classes.
Legal Weapon Against Copycats
Send takedowns and sue infringers with a registered right behind you.
Marketplace Brand Registry
Amazon and other platforms unlock brand protection tools for trademark owners.
Business Asset
A trademark can be valued, licensed, franchised and sold.
Customer Trust
The R mark signals an established, serious brand.
documents: Brand name and logo in JPEG format
Applicant PAN and Aadhaar (or incorporation certificate for entities)
Description of goods or services offered under the brand
Signed authorisation (Form TM-48) for filing
MSME or startup certificate for fee concession, if available
Date of first use with proof, if the brand is already in use
process: Availability Search
We search identical and similar marks in the registry and give you an honest risk view.
Class Selection
The correct classes are chosen from all 45 so protection actually covers your business.
Application Filing
The application is filed online; you can start using TM the same day.
Examination Follow Up
We track the examination report and respond to objections if raised.
Registration
After acceptance and publication, the registration certificate is issued and the R mark is yours.
timeline: Filing in 1 to 2 days; registration typically 8 to 18 months if unopposed
authority: Trade Marks Registry, Government of India
fees_note: Government fee is lower for individuals, startups and MSMEs per class
why_us: A cheap filing without a real search is how objections happen. Our search reports tell you the risks before you spend, and our filings are built to survive examination.
faqs: What is the difference between TM and R symbols?
TM can be used as soon as an application is filed and claims the mark. R can be used only after registration and carries full statutory protection. Using R without registration is an offence.
Should I register the name, the logo or both?
A wordmark protects the name in any styling; a logo mark protects the design. If budget allows one, the wordmark usually protects more. We advise based on how your brand is actually used.
What happens if someone objects to my application?
The examiner may raise objections or a third party may oppose after publication. Both have structured reply processes with deadlines. Our team drafts responses and represents you at hearings.
Can I trademark a name that is already in use by someone else?
If someone has prior rights in the same or similar business, registration is risky and can invite disputes. That is exactly what our pre filing search evaluates, before you invest in branding.

name: Trademark Objection Reply
meta_title: Trademark Objection Reply | Response to Examination Report
meta_description: Received a trademark examination report? Expert replies to section 9 and 11 objections with case law and evidence, filed within the 30 day deadline.
excerpt: Professionally drafted replies to examination report objections, filed within the deadline with evidence and precedent.
intro: A trademark objection is not a rejection; it is the examiner asking why your mark should be registered. Most objections can be overcome, but only with a well argued reply filed within the deadline of the examination report.

Eaccountingcart drafts objection replies with legal grounds, precedent and user evidence, then follows the application through hearing if required. WhatsApp your examination report for a free assessment.
what: Objections typically arise under section 9 (mark is descriptive or lacks distinctiveness) or section 11 (similar marks already exist) of the Trade Marks Act. The reply must address each ground with arguments and evidence such as proof of use, sales figures and distinctiveness acquired. If the examiner is not convinced on paper, a hearing is scheduled where the case is argued in person.
who: Applicants who received an examination report with objections
Businesses whose earlier reply was rejected and a hearing is fixed
Applicants whose deadline is near and need urgent drafting
Brand owners who filed themselves and hit unexpected objections
benefits: Deadline Rescue
Replies drafted and filed within the statutory 30 day window.
Ground Specific Arguments
Section 9 and section 11 objections need different strategies; we apply the right one.
Evidence Building
Invoices, ads and sales data are compiled into a persuasive user affidavit.
Hearing Representation
If the matter reaches a hearing, our team argues it for you.
Honest Assessment
If a mark is genuinely weak, we say so and suggest fixes before you spend more.
documents: Examination report received from the registry
Original application details
Proof of use: invoices, packaging, ads, website and social media
Sales and marketing spend figures year wise, if available
Any media coverage or awards for the brand
Authorisation for representation (TM-48)
process: Report Analysis
We decode the exact objections and assess the strength of your position.
Evidence Collection
Use and reputation evidence is gathered and organised into exhibits.
Reply Drafting
A legal reply addressing each ground with precedent is drafted for your approval.
Filing
The response is filed online within the deadline.
Hearing Support
If listed for hearing, we prepare submissions and appear on your behalf.
timeline: Reply due within 30 days of the examination report
authority: Trade Marks Registry, Government of India
validity: Until the application is accepted or refused
fees_note: No government fee for the reply itself
why_us: Objection replies are legal drafting, not form filling. Our replies argue distinctiveness and dissimilarity the way examiners evaluate them, which is why our acceptance rate stays high.
faqs: What happens if I miss the reply deadline?
The application is marked abandoned. A fresh application means new fees and a later priority date, which can be fatal if competitors filed meanwhile. If your deadline is close, contact us today.
My mark is objected as 'descriptive'. Is it over?
No. Descriptive marks can be registered by proving acquired distinctiveness through long use, sales and advertising evidence. This is one of the most common objections we overcome.
The examiner cited similar existing marks. What now?
We compare goods, channels and visual or phonetic differences, and where possible obtain consent or argue honest concurrent use. Many cited marks turn out to be dead or unrelated on analysis.
Do I need to attend the hearing myself?
No. With an authorisation on record, our representative attends and argues the matter. You stay informed at every stage without visiting the registry.

name: Trademark Opposition
meta_title: Trademark Opposition | File or Defend an Opposition in India
meta_description: File an opposition against a conflicting trademark or defend your application against one. Notices, counter statements, evidence and hearings handled end to end.
excerpt: Complete opposition support: stop conflicting marks from registering, or defend your own application against attack.
intro: After a trademark is accepted, it is published in the journal for four months, and anyone can oppose it. Opposition is how brand owners stop lookalikes before they become registered rights, and how applicants must defend what they filed.

Eaccountingcart handles both sides: filing oppositions against conflicting marks you spot, and defending your application when someone opposes it, through notices, counter statements, evidence rounds and hearings.
what: Opposition proceedings run before the Trade Marks Registry: a notice of opposition (TM-O) is filed within four months of journal publication; the applicant must file a counter statement within two months or the application is deemed abandoned; both sides then file evidence by affidavit, followed by a hearing and a decision.
who: Brand owners who found a similar mark published in the journal
Applicants served with a notice of opposition
Companies running brand watch on their trademarks
Prior users fighting a later applicant trying to register their name
benefits: Stop Copycats Early
Blocking a mark at opposition is far cheaper than litigation after registration.
Deadline Protection
Every stage has strict, largely unextendable timelines that we track for you.
Strong Pleadings
Notices and counter statements drafted with the grounds that actually win.
Evidence by Affidavit
Use, reputation and confusion evidence compiled to registry standards.
Negotiated Outcomes
Where sensible, we negotiate coexistence or withdrawal to save years of fighting.
documents: Journal publication details of the conflicting mark (for opposing)
Notice of opposition received (for defending)
Your registration or application details
Evidence of use: invoices, promotions, sales figures
Any correspondence with the other side
Authorisation for representation
process: Case Evaluation
We assess the strength of the opposition or defence honestly before you commit.
Pleadings
The notice of opposition or counter statement is drafted and filed within deadline.
Evidence Rounds
Affidavit evidence is prepared, filed and exchanged as per the rules.
Hearing
Our team argues the matter at the registry hearing.
Decision and Beyond
We advise on the order, including appeal or settlement options.
timeline: Opposition window: 4 months from publication; proceedings run 1 to 3 years
authority: Trade Marks Registry, Government of India
fees_note: Government fee applies per notice of opposition
why_us: Oppositions are won on pleadings and evidence discipline. We run a docketed process where no deadline slips, because in opposition, a missed date is a lost case.
faqs: How do I know if someone filed a mark similar to mine?
Through journal watching. We run brand watch for clients and alert you when confusingly similar marks are published, while the opposition window is still open.
What happens if I do not respond to an opposition against my application?
Failing to file the counter statement within two months means your application is treated as abandoned. There is no revival, so respond immediately.
Can opposition disputes be settled?
Yes. Many end in coexistence agreements, amendments to goods descriptions or withdrawal. We negotiate where settlement serves you better than years of proceedings.
Is opposition the same as court litigation?
No. Opposition is an administrative proceeding at the registry and far more economical. Court comes into play for infringement actions or appeals from registry decisions.

name: Trademark Renewal
meta_title: Trademark Renewal Online | Renew Before Expiry
meta_description: Renew your trademark for another 10 years before expiry. Late renewal and restoration of removed marks also handled. WhatsApp your registration number.
excerpt: Keep your registered brand alive with timely 10 year renewals, or restore a mark that has lapsed.
intro: A registered trademark lasts ten years, and an expired one is an open invitation to competitors. Renewal is simple when done on time; after expiry it becomes costlier and, past the restoration window, the mark can be lost entirely.

Eaccountingcart renews trademarks before deadlines, handles late renewals with surcharge and files restoration for marks already removed. We also maintain a renewal calendar so your brand never lapses again.
what: Trademark renewal is filed in form TM-R, ideally within one year before expiry. After expiry, renewal with surcharge is possible for six months. Beyond that, a removed mark can be restored within one year of expiry through a restoration application with renewal fees. Each renewal extends protection for ten years.
who: Owners of trademarks approaching the 10 year mark
Businesses that discovered a lapsed registration
Companies holding portfolios of marks across classes
Assignees who acquired marks and need to maintain them
benefits: Uninterrupted Protection
Renewal on time keeps your exclusive rights seamless.
No Surcharge Costs
Timely filing avoids late fees and restoration expenses.
Portfolio Calendar
All your marks tracked in one renewal schedule with advance reminders.
Restoration Expertise
Lapsed marks recovered within the legal window with proper grounds.
Updated Records
Ownership and address records corrected during renewal where needed.
documents: Trademark registration number and certificate copy
Applicant PAN or entity incorporation proof
Power of attorney (TM-48) for filing
Assignment deed if ownership changed
Previous renewal receipts, if any
process: Status Check
We verify the mark's current status and exact renewal window on the registry.
Document Collection
Basic ownership documents are collected on WhatsApp.
Renewal Filing
TM-R is filed with the correct fee, with surcharge or restoration where applicable.
Certificate Tracking
The renewal is tracked until the registry updates the register.
Calendar Setup
Your next renewal dates go into our reminder system automatically.
timeline: Filing in 1 to 2 days; registry processing a few weeks
authority: Trade Marks Registry, Government of India
fees_note: Government fee per class; surcharge applies after expiry
why_us: Most lapses happen because nobody was watching the date. Our clients' marks sit in a monitored renewal calendar, so the ten year deadline is our problem, not yours.
faqs: When can I file for renewal?
Any time within one year before the expiry date. Filing early carries no downside, the new term still runs from the expiry date.
My trademark expired last month. Is it gone?
No. For six months after expiry you can renew with a surcharge, and within one year a restoration application can revive a removed mark. Beyond that, refiling from scratch is usually the only route.
Do I need to prove use at renewal?
No use proof is needed for renewal itself. However, a mark unused for five years or more becomes vulnerable to cancellation by others, which is worth discussing if you have stopped using it.
Can renewal update my company's new name or address?
Renewal and recordal are separate filings. We file the necessary TM-P recordals along with renewal so the register reflects current ownership details.

name: Trademark Assignment
meta_title: Trademark Assignment | Transfer Trademark Ownership Legally
meta_description: Transfer or acquire trademark ownership with a proper assignment deed and registry recordal. Deed drafting, TM-P filing and follow up by experts.
excerpt: Transfer trademark ownership with a legally sound deed and complete recordal before the registry.
intro: Trademarks are property: they can be sold, gifted or transferred in a business acquisition. But the transfer is complete only when a proper assignment deed exists and the registry records the new owner. Skipping recordal leaves the buyer unable to enforce the mark.
Eaccountingcart drafts assignment deeds that hold up, values the consideration correctly for stamp duty and completes the TM-P recordal so the register shows the rightful owner.
what: Assignment under the Trade Marks Act can be with or without the goodwill of the business, complete or partial by goods or territory. The deed must be stamped as per state law, and the assignee applies for recordal in form TM-P with the deed. Restrictions apply to assignments that would create confusion, such as parallel rights in the same goods.
who: Businesses buying or selling brands or product lines
Founders moving personal trademarks into their company
Family businesses restructuring ownership of marks
Companies in mergers or acquisitions with trademark portfolios
benefits: Enforceable Ownership
A recorded assignment lets the new owner sue infringers and license the mark.
Clean Deal Documentation
Deeds drafted with warranties and goodwill clauses that prevent later disputes.
Correct Stamp Duty
Consideration and duty are handled correctly, an area that often invalidates deeds.
Registry Recordal
TM-P filed and tracked until the register reflects the assignee.
Portfolio Transfers
Multi mark, multi class transfers coordinated in one engagement.
documents: Trademark registration or application details
PAN and incorporation documents of assignor and assignee
Details of consideration and whether goodwill is included
Board resolutions approving the transfer, for companies
No objection from the assignor
Existing license agreements affecting the mark, if any
process: Transaction Review
We confirm what is being transferred, with or without goodwill, full or partial.
Deed Drafting
The assignment deed is drafted with warranties, executed and stamped correctly.
TM-P Filing
The recordal application is filed with the registry along with the deed.
Registry Follow Up
We respond to any registry query until the assignee is recorded.
Post Transfer Steps
Renewal calendars and license records are updated for the new owner.
timeline: Deed in 3 to 5 days; recordal takes a few months at the registry
authority: Trade Marks Registry, Government of India
fees_note: Government fee per mark plus applicable stamp duty on the deed
why_us: We handle both the legal deed and the tax angles of brand transfers, capital gains and stamp duty included, which pure IP agents miss and pure tax firms do not draft.
faqs: What does assignment 'with goodwill' mean?

With goodwill, the buyer acquires the brand along with the business reputation attached to it and can use it for the same goods. Without goodwill, use is restricted and additional conditions apply, including advertisement requirements.
Can a pending application be assigned?
Yes, both registered marks and pending applications can be assigned. The recordal process differs slightly, and we handle both.
Is assignment taxable?
The assignor may have capital gains, and GST can apply to the transfer depending on structure. As a CA firm we plan the transaction to be tax efficient before the deed is signed.
What if the registry record still shows the old owner?
Until recordal, the assignee's ability to enforce and renew is compromised. If you bought a mark years ago without recordal, we can still file TM-P with the deed and affidavits now.

name: Trademark Rectification
meta_title: Trademark Rectification | Remove or Correct a Registered Mark
meta_description: File rectification to remove a wrongly registered or unused trademark, or defend your registration against removal. Expert petitions and representation.
excerpt: Challenge wrongly registered or unused marks, or defend your own registration in rectification proceedings.
intro: Registration is not always the end of the story. A mark obtained wrongly, or left unused for years, can be removed from the register through rectification. Equally, your own registration can be attacked, and must be defended.
Eaccountingcart files and defends rectification petitions: petitions to remove blocking marks that were wrongly granted or never used, and defences that keep your registration alive.
what: Rectification under sections 47 and 57 of the Trade Marks Act allows an aggrieved person to seek removal or variation of a registered mark, on grounds such as registration without sufficient cause, non use for five years and three months, or entries made by fraud. Petitions are filed before the Trade Marks Registry or High Court, followed by evidence and hearing.
who: Businesses blocked by a registered mark that is not actually in use
Prior users whose name was registered by someone else
Registrants served with a rectification petition
Applicants whose registration cites a dormant conflicting mark
benefits: Clear the Path
Removing a dead or wrongly granted mark can unblock your own registration.
Non Use Strategy
Marks unused for the statutory period are removable, a powerful, underused remedy.
Defence Expertise
If your mark is attacked, we build the use and validity evidence to defend it.
Forum Selection
We choose between registry and High Court routes based on your case.
Litigation Support
Coordinated strategy if parallel infringement disputes are running.
documents: Details of the mark sought to be rectified or defended
Your trademark applications or registrations affected
Evidence of the other side's non use or bad faith, where available
Your own use evidence: invoices, promotions, sales data
Correspondence or legal notices exchanged
Authorisation for representation
process: Merits Assessment
We investigate the target mark's use and history and advise candidly on prospects.
Petition Drafting
The rectification petition or counter is drafted with grounds and supporting affidavits.
Filing
The matter is filed before the appropriate forum with fees.
Evidence and Hearing
Affidavits are exchanged and the matter argued at hearing.
Order Implementation
We follow the order through to actual register correction.
why_us: Rectification is investigation plus advocacy. We build the factual record, market checks, archived web evidence, filing histories, that makes non use and bad faith arguments stick.
faqs: When can a mark be removed for non use?
If it has not been used for a continuous period of five years and three months before the petition, it is vulnerable to removal. Token or fake use does not save it.
Someone registered my brand name before I could. Any remedy?
Yes. If you are the prior user, rectification on grounds of registration without cause or bad faith is available, supported by your use evidence. Timelines matter, so act quickly.
Can rectification and opposition happen together?
Opposition applies before registration; rectification after. If you missed the opposition window, rectification is usually the remedy against a now registered mark.
How do I protect my own mark from non use attacks?
Use it genuinely and keep dated evidence: invoices, ads, packaging. For marks in portfolio storage, we advise on maintaining defensible use.

name: International Trademark Registration
meta_title: International Trademark Registration | Madrid Protocol Filing
meta_description: Protect your brand abroad through the Madrid Protocol from your Indian base application. Country strategy, filing and objection handling worldwide.
excerpt: Take your brand global through a single Madrid Protocol filing covering the countries you choose.
intro: If you export, sell online internationally or plan to expand abroad, your Indian trademark stops at the border. International registration through the Madrid Protocol extends protection to over 100 countries through one application.

Eaccountingcart plans your country strategy, files the international application through the Indian registry and manages objections raised by foreign offices, all coordinated from one point of contact.
what: The Madrid Protocol allows an Indian applicant with a base application or registration to file one international application through the Indian Trade Marks Registry, designating member countries. WIPO records the mark and each designated country examines it under its own law within set timelines. Fees depend on countries and classes chosen.
who: Exporters selling branded goods abroad
SaaS and service companies with international customers
Brands on global marketplaces like Amazon in the US or UAE markets
Businesses planning franchises or distributors overseas
benefits: One Application, Many Countries
A single filing in one language with one set of fees covers all designated members.
Cost Efficiency
Substantially cheaper than filing separately through attorneys in each country.
Central Management
Renewals and ownership changes update all countries through WIPO in one step.
Expansion Ready
New countries can be added later through subsequent designation.
Priority Protection
Claiming priority from your Indian filing protects your date abroad.
documents: Indian trademark application or registration details (base mark)
List of countries where protection is needed
Goods and services description matching the base mark
Applicant details identical to the Indian filing
Power of attorney where individual countries require it
process: Country Strategy
We shortlist countries based on your sales, manufacturing and expansion plans, with a fee estimate.
Base Mark Check
The Indian base application is verified, since the international mark depends on it for five years.
MM2 Filing
The international application is filed through the Indian registry to WIPO.
National Phase Monitoring
Each country's acceptance or objection is tracked and responses coordinated.
Grant and Maintenance
Registrations are recorded and renewals managed centrally.
timeline: WIPO processing 2 to 6 months; country examinations 12 to 18 months
authority: WIPO via the Indian Trade Marks Registry
fees_note: Fees in Swiss Francs depend on countries and classes designated
why_us: Choosing countries poorly wastes lakhs; ignoring the base mark dependency can sink the whole portfolio. We plan both, and coordinate foreign objections without you hiring separate attorneys blind.
faqs: Do I need an Indian trademark first?
Yes. The Madrid route requires an Indian application or registration as the base. Your international rights depend on that base mark for the first five years.
What if one country objects to my mark?
Each country examines independently, so an objection in one does not affect others. Local responses are required; we coordinate this through our associate network.
Is the Madrid Protocol always the best route?
Mostly, but for one or two countries, direct national filings are sometimes cheaper or strategically better, for example where local use requirements are strict. We compare both routes for you.
What is 'central attack'?

If the Indian base mark fails within five years, the international registration falls with it, though conversions to national filings are possible. This is why we secure the base mark before going international.

name: Copyright Registration
meta_title: Copyright Registration Online | Protect Creative Work in India
meta_description: Register copyright for books, music, software, art and videos. Complete filing with the Copyright Office, objections handled. Share your work details today.
excerpt: Register your creative work, from software and books to music and art, and get certificate proof of ownership.
intro: Copyright protects what you create: writing, software code, music, films, art and more. While copyright exists automatically on creation, a registration certificate is the proof that wins disputes, licensing deals and takedown battles.
Eaccountingcart files copyright applications with the Copyright Office, prepares the work copies in the required format and responds to objections until the certificate is issued.
what: Copyright registration under the Copyright Act, 1957 covers literary works (including software), artistic works, musical works, sound recordings and cinematograph films. Applications are filed in form XIV per work with copies of the work; after a mandatory waiting period for objections, the office examines and registers the work, typically granting protection for the author's life plus sixty years.
who: Software companies protecting source code
Authors, bloggers and course creators
Musicians, producers and video creators
Designers and artists whose work is copied online
Businesses protecting website content, manuals and training material
benefits: Court Ready Proof
The certificate is prima facie evidence of ownership in any dispute.
Monetisation Basis
Licensing, publishing and distribution deals stand on registered rights.
Takedown Power
Registered copyright accelerates platform takedowns of copied content.
Long Protection
Rights last the author's lifetime plus sixty years.
Asset Creation
Registered works can be valued, assigned and inherited cleanly.
documents: Copies of the work (manuscript, code extract, artwork, audio or video files)
Author and owner details with PAN and address proof
No objection certificate from the author if the owner is different
NOC from publisher if the work is published
Power of attorney for filing
For artistic works used on goods: trademark search certificate where required
process: Work Classification
We identify the correct category and prepare the work copies in acceptable format.
Application Filing
Form XIV is filed online with the work and fees, and the diary number issued.
Waiting Period
The mandatory 30 day objection window is tracked.
Examination Response
Any discrepancy letter from the examiner is answered with corrections or clarifications.
Certificate
The registration certificate is issued and delivered to you.
timeline: 6 to 12 months including the objection window
validity: Author's life plus 60 years (for most works)
fees_note: Government fee varies by type of work
why_us: Applications stall on format issues, wrong category, incomplete work copies, missing NOCs. We prepare filings that clear examination, including tricky software and multi author works.
faqs: Is my work not protected without registration?
Copyright arises automatically on creation, but proving ownership and the creation date in a dispute is hard without registration. The certificate settles that question before it is asked.
Can I copyright my mobile app or website?
The source code registers as a literary work, and distinctive visual elements can register as artistic works. We typically protect software through code registration plus trademark for the name.
What is the difference between copyright and trademark?
Copyright protects creative expression, the content itself. Trademark protects brand identifiers in trade. A logo can enjoy both, and we often file both together.
Who owns copyright in work I paid a freelancer to create?
Without a written assignment, the creator often retains rights. We draft the assignment and file registration in your name, closing that gap.

name: Patent Registration
meta_title: Patent Registration in India | Provisional and Complete Filing
meta_description: Protect your invention with expert patentability search, drafting and filing. Provisional and complete specifications, examination responses and grant support.
excerpt: From patentability search to grant: professional drafting and prosecution of your patent application in India.
intro: A patent gives you twenty years of exclusive rights over your invention, the strongest protection intellectual property law offers. It is also the most technical to obtain: claims drafted poorly protect nothing, even if granted.
Eaccountingcart coordinates the full patent journey with experienced patent professionals: prior art search, provisional and complete specification drafting, filing, examination responses and grant.
what: Patents under the Patents Act, 1970 protect inventions that are new, involve an inventive step and have industrial application. A provisional application secures your date while the invention is refined; the complete specification with claims must follow within twelve months. After publication and a request for examination, the office issues examination reports that must be answered before grant.
who: Inventors and engineers with new products or processes
Startups building defensible technology
Manufacturers improving machines, materials or methods
Research driven businesses and institutions
benefits: 20 Year Monopoly
Exclusive rights to make, use and sell the invention in India.
Investor Signal
Filed patents materially strengthen startup valuations and funding conversations.
Licensing Revenue
Patents can be licensed or sold as standalone assets.
Early Date Security
A provisional filing locks your priority date while development continues.
Startup Concessions
Recognised startups get major fee rebates and expedited examination.
documents: Detailed description of the invention and how it works
Drawings, diagrams or flowcharts
Details of the problem solved and advantages over existing solutions
Inventor and applicant details with proof
Any prior publications or disclosures made
Assignment from inventors if a company is applying
process: Patentability Search
Prior art is searched worldwide and you get an honest opinion on novelty before spending on drafting.
Specification Drafting
Provisional or complete specification with claims is drafted by patent professionals.
Filing
The application is filed with the Indian Patent Office with applicable concessions.
Publication and Examination
We request examination and respond to office actions and objections.
Grant and Maintenance
On grant, we set up the annuity calendar to keep the patent alive.
timeline: Filing quickly; grant typically 2 to 4 years (faster with expedited examination)
validity: 20 years from filing, subject to annual renewal fees
fees_note: Government fees are reduced for individuals, startups and MSMEs
why_us: The search opinion comes before the invoice for drafting. If your invention is not protectable, we tell you at the cheapest possible stage, and if it is, the claims are drafted to be enforced, not just granted.
faqs: Can I patent an idea?
Not an abstract idea, but a concrete implementation, a product, process or method that is new and inventive, can be patented. We help convert concepts into patentable descriptions.
What is the benefit of a provisional application?
It locks your priority date at lower cost while you refine the invention, giving twelve months to file the complete specification. In fast moving fields, that date is everything.
Is software patentable in India?

Software as such is excluded, but software combined with hardware or producing a technical effect can be protected with careful claim drafting. This is a specialised area where drafting quality decides the outcome.
What happens if I disclosed my invention publicly before filing?
Public disclosure before filing can destroy novelty, with narrow grace period exceptions. Talk to us before publishing, pitching or exhibiting your invention.

why_us: Design cases are lost on bad drawings and late filings. We prepare registry standard views fast, because in design law, whoever files first wins, and public disclosure can kill novelty.
faqs: Should I file before launching the product?
Yes. Prior publication, including your own marketing, can destroy novelty. File first, launch after; the filing itself is quick.
What is not protected by design registration?
Functional features, methods of construction and anything dictated purely by function fall outside design law. Those may need patent protection instead, which we assess together.
How is design different from trademark for a product shape?

Design protects a new shape for up to fifteen years; a shape trademark can last forever but demands proof that the shape identifies your brand. Many products start with design and graduate to shape marks.
Can I register variations of the same product?
Each distinct design registers separately, though sets and multiple embodiments have specific rules. We structure the filings to cover your product family economically.
